writeup: TIC 119941327 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 6.521291 days and a primary eclipse depth of 4.23 percent. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. Pixel-level analysis confirms the eclipse signal with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise ratio of 35.5, though the centroid offset of 2.4 arcseconds from the target warrants attention. A secondary eclipse was not detected. One open question remains: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the initial period measurement may have been affected by this variation, though the corrected period accounts for this effect and pixel-level confirmation remains robust.
